segments.text: If your dog ever smiles at you with human teeth... do not smile back.
Do not smile back. Do not let it eat from your plate. And never let it look in the mirror.
This is Protocol four zero four.
There are four rules. Follow them exactly. Otherwise, you will have to activate the emergency protocol.
Rule one. Do not smile back.
You come home. Your dog runs to the door, like always. Tail going. Ears back.
Then it smiles at you. Not a dog smile. A wide one. And behind its lips, there is a row of flat, white, human teeth.
Something has moved into your dog. It learns by copying the face it sees most. Yours. And that smile is not for you. It is a question.
It is asking if you are ready to trade places.
You will want to smile back. You have smiled at your dog every day of its life. Do not do it. A smile is a yes.
Keep your face still. Pet it. Say its name. Then walk away.
One owner smiled back. His dog stood up on its back legs, reached out, and patted him on the head. "Good boy," it said. In his voice.
Rule two. Do not let it eat from your plate.
Dinner time. It does not go to its bowl. It sits next to your chair. And watches your fork.
A real dog begs. This one is studying. How you hold the fork. How you chew. How long you wait between bites.
Do not give it a piece. Not even one. Every bite of your food teaches it what you are made of.
If you do, the next night, its bowl is still full. And the chair across from you has been pulled out.
It is sitting in it. Back straight. Paws on the table. Waiting for you to pass the salt.
Feed it in another room. Close the door. Eat fast.
Rule three. Never let it look in the mirror.
Dogs do not care about mirrors. Yours stops in front of the hallway mirror. And stays there.
It is checking its work. Comparing its teeth to yours.
Do not let it finish looking. Cover the mirror. Move it. Turn it to the wall.
Because the day it sees a face that matches yours, it stops being a dog.
In the mirror, where your dog is sitting, there is a person. On all fours. Smiling.
And it turns around. Slowly. To find out which one of you is the copy.
Rule four. Emergency protocol. How to fight back.
If you already smiled back, fed it from your plate, or let it see the mirror, the trade begins. And if you leave it alone, it finishes.
Three A.M. You wake up on the floor. In the dog bed. Up on your bed, under your blanket, something is sleeping on your pillow.
And on the nightstand, there is a collar. With a name tag. Your name.
Here is what does not work.
Calling the vet. "His teeth are perfectly healthy. Healthier than yours."
Locking it outside. Thirty seconds later, the doorbell rings.
Hiding. It is still a dog. It can smell you anywhere in the house.

Fighting it. Do not even try. It has the body of a forty-kilo dog and the mind of a grown man. Before your hand comes down, it is already on your chest. Its human teeth stop one inch from your throat. And it smiles.
There is only one thing that works. Remember how it learned to be you. It copies you.
So give it something else to copy. Be the dog.
Get down on all fours. Pull your lips back. Show your teeth. And growl. Loud. Louder than it has ever heard you.
It hesitates. It has never seen you do this. Then it does what it always does. It copies you.
It drops to four legs. Its lips pull back. It growls back at you. And the more it copies a dog, the less room there is for you.
One by one, the human teeth fall out. Click. Click. Click. Onto the floor. Sharp dog teeth slide back in.
Bark. It barks. Scratch behind your ear. It scratches behind its ear. Do not stop until the last human tooth hits the floor.
Then ask the question only a real dog cannot answer. "Who's a good boy?"
It does not say "I am." It just wags its tail.
In the morning, your dog is asleep in its bed. Normal teeth. Normal dog.
You go to brush your teeth. You smile at the mirror.
Top row. Left side. One of your teeth is long, and sharp, and not yours.
It copied you. And for a few minutes last night... you copied it.
And that was Protocol four zero four.
If this ever happens to you... you know the protocol.
